title: Staying Up Past Midnight Might Make Us More Impulsive and Cynical
titleZh: 熬夜到凌晨，可能让人更冲动、更悲观
summary:
2022年，一组心理学家提出，熬夜会引起大脑发生某些变化，从而增加危险行为与健康损害的风险。换句话说，真正重要的可能不只是你睡了多久、睡得好不好，还包括你在什么时间入睡。这些研究人员在《网络心理学前沿》期刊上发表的文章中提出了“午夜后心智”假说。该假说认为，熬夜到凌晨会触发一系列神经生理层面的变化，从而影响人的行为模式，使个体变得更为冲动、更为消极，也更可能参与有害行为。

来源：Discover；作者：Rosie McCall；原文发布时间：2025-10-24 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: In 2022, a team of psychologists suggested burning the midnight oil could lead to changes in the brain associated with hazardous behaviors and harmful health outcomes. In essence, it might not just be how long or how well you sleep but when you squeeze in shut-eye that matters. Writing in the journal Frontiers in Network Psychology, the researchers outlined the “Mind After Midnight” hypothesis. The theory links staying up into the early hours to a series of neurophysiological changes that influence our behaviour, making us more impulsive, more cynical, and more likely to participate in harmful activities.
paragraphs.contentZh: 2022年，一组心理学家提出，熬夜会引起大脑发生某些变化，从而增加危险行为与健康损害的风险。换句话说，真正重要的可能不只是你睡了多久、睡得好不好，还包括你在什么时间入睡。这些研究人员在《网络心理学前沿》期刊上发表的文章中提出了“午夜后心智”假说。该假说认为，熬夜到凌晨会触发一系列神经生理层面的变化，从而影响人的行为模式，使个体变得更为冲动、更为消极，也更可能参与有害行为。

paragraphs.contentEn: There is some evidence for this reasoning. Research has found that the number of violent crime and homicides increase after dark, as does the risk of suicide and suicidal thinking. On a less extreme level, data suggests we are more at risk of obesity and more likely to indulge in unhealthy foods if we eat at night. A caveat: these studies don’t always separate nocturnal wakefulness from sleep loss. It is also worth noting that there may be other factors driving these behaviors, such as darkness providing a better cover for crime than daylight.
paragraphs.contentZh: 这一假说已有研究提供部分支持。研究发现，夜间暴力犯罪和凶杀案件的发生率有所上升，自杀风险以及出现自杀念头也在夜晚更为常见。在较不极端的层面上，数据显示，夜间进食可能增加肥胖风险，并使人更倾向于放纵自己摄入不健康食物。不过需要指出的是，这些研究并不总是明确区分“夜间清醒”与“睡眠不足”这两种状态。同样值得注意的是，某些行为背后可能还存在其他影响因素，例如黑暗环境相比白天更能为犯罪行为提供掩护。

paragraphs.contentEn: When the study was first published, lead author Elizabeth B. Klerman, Professor of Neurology at Harvard Medical School, called for more research into the phenomenon. “My plea is for more research to look at that, because their health and safety, as well as that of others, is affected,” she said in a press release. More recently, researchers examining the link between bedtimes and mental health have advised turning in before 1 a.m. — even if you are a self-described “night owl.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 这项研究发表时，其首席作者、哈佛大学医学院神经学教授伊丽莎白·B·克勒曼曾呼吁学界对此现象展开更多研究。她在一份新闻声明中表示：“我真心希望能有更多研究关注这一问题，因为这不仅关系到熬夜者自身的健康与安全，也可能影响他人。”近期，一些在研究就寝时间与心理健康关联的科研人员建议，人们最好在凌晨一点之前入睡——即便你自认为自己是“夜猫子”。

paragraphs.contentEn: The hypothesis is based on the idea that our brains are influenced by the circadianclock, which can alter the way we think and act over a 24-hour time period. The result is that we may be more cheerful in the morning, when we are designed to feel awake, and more gloomy at night, when our body is preparing for sleep.
paragraphs.contentZh: 这一假说的理论基础是：大脑会受到生物节律的影响，从而使我们的思维和行为模式在24小时的周期内发生变化。这就导致我们在清晨往往心情更愉悦，因为此时身体被设定为清醒状态；而到了夜晚，当身体开始为入睡做准备时，情绪则可能变得更加低落。

paragraphs.contentEn: The circadian clock can and does vary on an individual-to-individual basis, with some of us running a little ahead of schedule (morning larks) and some of us a little behind (night owls). But at a population level, most people in the U.S. can expect to feel their most awake between 10 a.m. and 8 p.m. and their least awake around 3 a.m. According to Klerman and co, negative bias could result in poor decision-making. This could be exacerbated by a surge in dopamine that impacts the reward and motivation system, increasing the possibility of risky behavior.
paragraphs.contentZh: 每个人的生物钟确实存在差异：有些人节奏略快（“早鸟型”），有些人则略慢（“夜猫子型”）。但从群体水平来看，美国的大多数人通常在上午10点到晚上8点之间最为清醒，在凌晨3点左右最为困倦。克勒曼及其团队指出，这种在夜间出现的“负面偏向”可能会导致判断失误。与此同时，多巴胺水平的激增会进一步放大这种影响——通过刺激大脑的奖赏与动机系统，从而增加人们从事冒险行为的可能性。

paragraphs.contentEn: Research has shown that general mood and well-being levels tend to be lower when the circadian rhythm is misaligned — a pattern seen in shift workers. Meanwhile, a paper published in Psychiatry Research detected a peak in “negative affect” (or low mood) at night, which the researchers suggest may help explain the link between depression and insomnia.
paragraphs.contentZh: 研究也已证明，当人体的昼夜节律出现紊乱时，整体情绪和幸福感水平往往会下降——这种情况在轮班工作者中尤为常见。此外，发表在《精神病学研究》期刊上的一项研究发现，人们的“负面情绪”（即低落情绪）会在夜间达到峰值。研究人员认为，这一现象或许能解释抑郁与失眠之间的关联。

paragraphs.contentEn: More recently, a 2024 study in Psychiatry Research found that those who go to bed early display better mental health — regardless of whether or not they consider themselves a morning lark or night owl. The researchers came to this conclusion after comparing sleeping patterns to rates of depression and anxiety in over 70,000 middle- and older-aged adults. They advised, “For healthy aging, it is recommended that individuals initiate their sleep before [1 a.m.], regardless of their chronobiological preferences.
paragraphs.contentZh: 2024年发表在《精神病学研究》期刊上的一项更近期的研究发现，较早入睡的人表现出更佳的心理健康状况——无论他们自我归类为“早鸟型”还是“夜猫子型”。研究团队通过对7万多名中老年人的睡眠模式与抑郁、焦虑发生率进行比较，得出了这一结论。研究人员据此建议：“为促进健康老龄化，无论个人的生物钟类型如何，都应尽量在凌晨1点前入睡。”

paragraphs.contentEn: Perhaps most intriguingly, the researchers of the paper found that it was not morning larks out of step with their preferences that experienced the worst outcomes, but night owls who were apparently in line with theirs. "If I had to hazard a guess, morning people who are up late are quite cognizant of the fact that their brain isn't working quite right, so they may put off making bad decisions," senior author Jamie Zeitzer, professor of psychiatry and behavioural sciences at Stanford Medicine, said in a statement. "Meanwhile, the evening person who is up late thinks, 'I'm feeling great. This is a great decision I'm making at 3 o'clock in the morning."
paragraphs.contentZh: 或许最耐人寻味的是，研究人员发现，出现不良结果的并不是那些违背自身作息偏好、被迫晚睡的“早鸟型”人群，而是那些晚睡行为与自身偏好一致的“夜猫子”。该研究的资深作者、斯坦福大学医学院精神病学与行为科学教授杰米·泽策在一份声明中表示：“如果让我猜测，我会认为，那些熬夜的早鸟能清醒地意识到自己此时大脑状态不佳，因此可能会避免做出糟糕的决定。相比之下，熬夜的夜猫子却会觉得，‘我状态好极了！凌晨三点做这个决定再合适不过了。’”
